study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Apply voxelwise normative modeling to T1-weighted MRI to map interindividual white matter volume (WMV) deviations across six psychiatric disorders and test whether heterogeneous deviations aggregate within common tracts, regions, or large-scale networks.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of deviation burden (Mann–Whitney U); voxel/tract/region/network overlap analyses with FDR correction; comparisons vs held-out controls (HCtest).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: WMV deviations are highly heterogeneous at the voxel level (overlap <8% within diagnoses) and less prevalent than GMV. Negative deviations aggregate within common tracts/regions/networks in ASD and SCZ (up to ~69%), but not consistently in ADHD, BP, MDD, or OCD.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Voxelwise extreme WMV deviations affected the same voxel in fewer than 8% of individuals with the same diagnosis. In ASD and SCZ, negative deviations showed significant aggregation within common tracts, regions, and large-scale networks (up to 69% of participants), whereas other disorders showed limited or no such aggregation. Positive WMV deviations were more common than negative across groups. Overall WMV deviation burden was lower than previously observed for GMV.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: WMV estimation via VBM may be limited by orientation-dependent white matter properties; diffusion MRI tractography has known false positives/negatives; reliance on DSM categories; lack of null models to disambiguate deviation burden vs selective targeting in WMV analyses.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: "... unlike gray matter, white matter’s fibrous bundles have a strong orientation dependence ... Combining registration tailored to white matter with tractography may provide greater specificity ..."; "Diffusion MRI ... struggles to accurately reconstruct tracts ... contributes to an inflated number of both false positives and false negatives ..."; "we used DSM diagnoses ... this reliance may limit the degree of observed neural overlap ..."; "WMV analyses lack such null models. Therefore, we cannot determine whether observed overlaps reflect differences in deviation burden or selective targeting ..."

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Train/test split: HCtrain=1196, HCtest=269; extreme deviation threshold |z|>2.6 with cluster size ≥10; multi-site cohort across 25 sites; site modeled as covariate.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: HC drawn from all clinical datasets plus MON (14 datasets, 25 sites). Modeling with PCNtoolkit v0.21 (warped BLR).
